(1) the bulk matter evolution and extraction method of jet transport coefficient in heavy-ion collisions are studied in this Letter, and the results are compared with the experimental data from RHIC; (2) we found that the jet transport parameter extracted from the experimental data is about 2.5 times smaller than the theoretical prediction; (3) we found that a large jet quenching parameter can be achieved in a very small window of time in the early stage of heavy-ion collisions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the extracted values of the jet transport coefficient in the medium created in heavy-ion collisions are in the range of 0.05-0.1, which is consistent with the theoretical predictions.
the jet quenching is a real and robust phenomenon, which is a result of the energy loss of partons in a dense medium, the quark-gluon plasma.
the jet transport parameter in the QGP medium extracted from the RHIC experimental data is 0.08 ± 0.01 GeV−2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have systematically investigated the evolution of bulk matter in Au+Au collisions at RHIC energies, and the extraction of jet transport coefficient in the medium formed in these collisions.
we study bulk matter evolution in high energy heavy ion collisions at the Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collider (RHIC) and extract the jet transport parameter in the quark-gluon plasma (QGP).
we study bulk matter evolution and extraction of jet transport parameter in relativistic heavy-ion collisions at the Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collider (RHIC).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jet transport parameter q is not a constant in heavy-ion collisions.
the jet transport parameter, q, can be extracted by comparing the bulk properties (such as the energy density) of the medium created in p+p collisions and in Au+Au collisions.
the bulk matter evolution and the extracted jet transport parameter in Au + Au collisions at RHIC are very sensitive to the equation of state.
